``` python
import rustymath as rm
```

## Minimization and scalar roots

`rm.optimize` takes SciPy’s names. `minimize` runs Brent’s method,
Nelder–Mead, Powell’s method, L-BFGS or differential evolution. Without
a `method`, it picks one from the number of variables, whether `jac`
gives a gradient and whether there are bounds. `root_scalar` finds a
zero of a function of one variable by Brent’s method, within a bracket
or by stepping outward from a start. Here Nelder–Mead finds the minimum
of Rosenbrock’s function, at (1, 1), and Brent’s method finds where cos
x = x:

``` python
rosen = lambda x: (1-x[0])**2 + 100*(x[1]-x[0]**2)**2
rm.optimize.minimize(rosen, [-1.2, 1]).x, rm.optimize.root_scalar(lambda x: rm.cos(x) - x, [0, 1]).root
```

    (Array([1.0, 1.0], dtype=float64), 0.7390851350713886)

`jac` supplies the gradient. Here, supplying it selects L-BFGS. Results
report the best point, its objective value, the number of evaluations
and whether the stopping test passed:

``` python
rosen_grad = lambda x: [-2*(1-x[0]) - 400*x[0]*(x[1]-x[0]**2), 200*(x[1]-x[0]**2)]
minimum = rm.optimize.minimize(rosen, [-1.2, 1], jac=rosen_grad)
minimum.x, minimum.fun, minimum.nfev, minimum.success
```

    (Array([1.0, 1.0], dtype=float64), 2.6802658590531843e-27, 53, True)

Differential evolution searches within finite bounds. `popsize` sets the
number of population members per variable; `maxfev` caps objective
evaluations, including polishing. With `vectorized=True`, the objective
receives an array of shape `(variables, candidates)` and returns one
value per column. Rosenbrock’s expression works unchanged on both single
points and columns. `seed` selects the random sequence:

``` python
bounded = rm.optimize.minimize(rosen, [-1.2, 1], method='differential-evolution',
    bounds=[(-2, 2), (-1, 3)], vectorized=True, options={'seed': 7, 'popsize': 8, 'maxfev': 2000})
bounded.x, bounded.fun, bounded.nfev, bounded.success
```

    (Array([1.0, 1.0], dtype=float64), 3.404388655577681e-16, 1465, True)

## Fitting residuals

`least_squares` fits residuals by Levenberg–Marquardt. `jac` returns a
Jacobian with one row per residual and one column per parameter.
Omitting it uses forward differences. Here the fit recovers a = 2 and b
= 0.3 from five points on y = a e^(bx):

``` python
t = rm.array([0., 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2])
residuals = lambda p: p[0]*rm.exp(p[1]*t) - 2*rm.exp(0.3*t)
jacobian = lambda p: rm.stack([rm.exp(p[1]*t), p[0]*t*rm.exp(p[1]*t)], axis=1)
fit = rm.optimize.least_squares(residuals, [1, 1], jac=jacobian)
fit.x, fit.cost, fit.success
```

    (Array([2.0, 0.3], dtype=float64), 3.468843267386382e-27, True)

## Matrix-free linear systems

The linear solvers take an array or an operator with `shape` and
`matvec`, such as a SciPy `LinearOperator`. Arrays run their products in
Rust. Operators supply products without storing the matrix.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Solver</th>
<th>Matrix requirement</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>cg</code></td>
<td>Symmetric positive definite</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>minres</code></td>
<td>Symmetric</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>gmres</code></td>
<td>General square</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cgls</code>, <code>lsmr</code></td>
<td>Rectangular or square; operators also supply <code>rmatvec</code>
for transpose products</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`cgls` applies CG to the normal equations without forming A.T @ A.
`lsmr` uses MINRES on the normal equations. `cgls` is not a Golub–Kahan
LSQR implementation.

`M` approximates the inverse matrix, or the inverse of A.T @ A for least
squares. It must be symmetric positive definite except with `gmres`.
GMRES applies `M` on the right, solving A M y = b and returning x = M y.
SciPy’s GMRES uses left preconditioning.

This operator fits a line without constructing its five-by-two design
matrix. The inverse diagonal of A.T @ A is a preconditioner. `normr`
reports the residual norm even when no line fits exactly:

``` python
positions = rm.arange(5, dtype='float64')
operator = SimpleNamespace(shape=(5, 2), matvec=lambda v: v[0] + v[1]*positions,
    rmatvec=lambda u: [rm.sum(u), rm.sum(positions*u)])
preconditioner = rm.diag([1/len(positions), 1/rm.sum(positions**2)])
line = rm.optimize.cgls(operator, [1., 2.9, 5.2, 6.8, 9.1], M=preconditioner)
line.x, line.normr, line.nmatvec, line.success
```

    (Array([0.98, 2.01], dtype=float64), 0.31464265445104594, 8, True)
